title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for six months after Fargo, North Dakota police wrongly charged her with bank theft. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee when the fraud occurred. Lipps was released on Christmas Eve and later learned she had lost her home, car, and personal property.

Lipps has filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million in damages from the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck. The suit alleges that police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and a surveillance video, even though Lipps did not resemble the suspect and had never been to North Dakota. It says Heck requested an arrest warrant without further investigation or probable cause. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit seeks accountability and hopes to encourage police to use facial recognition technology more carefully.
